newsitem.title: UK: Br Midland picks IAE engines.
newsitem.headline: Br Midland picks IAE engines.

text.p: Privately-owned airline British Midland Airways said on Friday it had picked International Aero Engines (IAE) to power its new fleet of 20 Airbus Industrie A320 and A321 twinjets.
IAE is jointly owned by Rolls-Royce Plc, United Technologies' Pratt & Whitney, Japanese Aero Engines Corp and Daimler-Benz AG unit MTU.
British Midland said the engines would be built by Rolls-Royce's plant at Derby, England, and the business was worth over $40 million to the British company, which has a one-third share of IAE.
British Midland, which is 40 percent owned by Scandinavian Airline Systems, announced the $1 billion order for the aircraft in April, with deliveries due over five years, starting next year.

The Airbus consortium comprises Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale of France, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
